Config files that point a coding agent at the model this server is serving now, with its context and capabilities filled in. They're a snapshot: download again after serving another model or changing its context size.

This address only works on this machine. If the agent runs elsewhere, change it to one that machine can reach (and set the External URL on the Settings page to make that the default).

Model in the files: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 — 131072 context, tools, reasoning

This server requires an API key. The files read it from VLLM_TOOLCHEST_API_KEY, so set that where the agent runs, to the key you set on the Settings page: 

export VLLM_TOOLCHEST_API_KEY='your API key'

Commands below are for a Linux or macOS shell; on Windows, set the same variables in PowerShell ($env:NAME = "value").

opencode — vllm-toolchest.opencode.json

Download vllm-toolchest.opencode.json opencode docs ↗

Save it in:

Linux~/.config/opencode/
macOS~/.config/opencode/
Windows%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\

Then:

export OPENCODE_CONFIG=~/.config/opencode/vllm-toolchest.opencode.json

OPENCODE_CONFIG layers this file over your own opencode.json, so nothing of yours is replaced. Add the export to your shell profile to make it stick.

Kilo Code — kilo.json

Download kilo.json Kilo Code docs ↗

Save it in:

Linux~/.config/kilo/
macOS~/.config/kilo/
Windows%USERPROFILE%\.config\kilo\

Kilo merges this with a kilo.json in your project, if you have one. If you already have a ~/.config/kilo/kilo.json, copy the "provider" block into it instead.

pi — models.json

Download models.json pi docs ↗

Save it in:

Linux~/.pi/agent/
macOS~/.pi/agent/
Windows%USERPROFILE%\.pi\agent\

If you already have a models.json, copy the "vllm-toolchest" entry into its "providers" instead of replacing the file.

Pick the model with /model in pi.

Goose — vllm_toolchest.json

Download vllm_toolchest.json Goose docs ↗

Save it in:

Linux~/.config/goose/custom_providers/
macOS~/.config/goose/custom_providers/
Windows%APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\custom_providers\

Then:

goose session --provider vllm_toolchest

Or choose vllm-toolchest in goose configure to make it the default.

Goose relies on tool calling: use a model that supports tools.

Crush — vllm-toolchest.crushrc

Download vllm-toolchest.crushrc Crush docs ↗

Save it in:

Linux~/.config/crush/
macOS~/.config/crush/
Windows%USERPROFILE%\.config\crush\

Then:

echo 'source ~/.config/crush/vllm-toolchest.crushrc' >> ~/.config/crush/crushrc

The source line keeps your own crushrc as it is; re-downloading this file updates the model without editing it again.
